subject: Game Theory
title: Vickrey's Truth Machine
description: A micro-lesson that makes Vickrey's Truth Machine usable.

hook.text: In a Vickrey auction, you bid your true value and win at the second-highest price. Lying can't help you.

buildup.text: If you bid higher than your value, you might win and overpay. Bid lower, you might lose when you shouldn't.

discovery.text: The dominant strategy: bid exactly what the item is worth to you. The mechanism makes honesty optimal.

twist.text: Google uses a generalized Vickrey auction for ad placements—each advertiser pays the bid of the next one below.

climax.text: William Vickrey won the Nobel Prize in 1996 for this insight, dying just three days after the announcement.

punchline.text: When the rules are right, honesty is free.

quiz.question: Why is honesty the best strategy in a Vickrey auction?
options: You pay the second-highest price so lying can only hurt you
